text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Amsterdam airport Schiphol buys 16 pct stake in privatised airport of Brisbane, Australia. (p1)
- Total market capitalisation of Amsterdam Stock Exchange listed companies tops trillion guilder threshold. (p1)
- Industry speculation mounts on imminent sale of brewer Grolsch. (p1)
- Dutch carrier KLM's decision to halt transport of radioactive materials affects three suppliers. (p3)
- Runaway demand for shares on Amsterdam bourse shows no signs of abating, with investors subscribing blindly to IPOs. (p1)
- Dutch seek to boost sales of electric cars through tax exemptions which could cut purchase prices by 40 pct. (p2)
- PTT Telecom monopoly on fixed-line telephony ends today (p2)
- Tank storage firm Van Ommeren to invest 60 million guilders to take 50 pct stake in Indian sector rival. (p.25)
- Poll shows some 60 percent of mobile phone users in private sector are dissatisfied with the service. (p.25)
- Traffic ministry knew Schiphol was growing faster than forecast at the time parliament set limits on the airport's growth, Schiphol president Hans Smits says in interview. (p1)
- Shipyard Wilton-Fijenoord saved from likely bankruptcy due to restructuring activities of the last two years. (p13)
